fixes.explanation: Close to something that shows up later, but not here. The counting comes at the end, where the text says about five thousand men were fed, besides women and children (Matthew 14:21). In verse 14, Jesus healed their sick.
Not this time, friend. The text says He had compassion on them and healed their sick (Matthew 14:14). He sees the crowd, and the healing follows.

Good thought, but no. Jesus said, “They do not need to go away…” and then, “You give them something to eat.” (Matthew 14:16) That “You” was Jesus answering the disciples, the ones who had just spoken to Him.

Yes, friend. The disciples answered, “We have here only five loaves of bread and two fish…” (Matthew 14:17) Notice that word “only.” I bet that's the sound of someone who did the math and doesn't love the result.
Not quite, friend. Here the disciples say, “We have here only five loaves of bread and two fish…” (Matthew 14:17) Five loaves and two fish, no more. I've seen a bigger stash in my own cookie jar.

Close on the idea, friend. The disciples say they have “…only five loaves of bread and two fish…” (Matthew 14:17) It was five loaves and two fish, not two loaves and one fish. Still a tiny amount for that crowd, but it was what they said they had.

Right, friend. Matthew says Jesus directed the crowds to sit down on the grass, and then He took the loaves and the fish (Matthew 14:19). That direction came before a single piece of bread went out. It's like clearing the counter before the baking starts.

That's it, friend. He took the loaves and the fish, looked up to heaven, and spoke a blessing (Matthew 14:19). The blessing came before He broke the loaves and gave them out. That's a good habit for any kitchen.

Zion doesn't show up in this passage, friend. The text says Jesus took the five loaves and the two fish, looked up to heaven, and spoke a blessing (Matthew 14:19). Heaven is the word that fits the blank.
Sinai doesn't show up in this passage, friend. Matthew says Jesus looked up to heaven and spoke a blessing over the loaves and fish (Matthew 14:19). Heaven is the word that fits the blank.

Jesus did direct the crowds to sit down on the grass (Matthew 14:19), but “rested” isn't the word in this verse. Matthew says they all ate and were satisfied (Matthew 14:20). Those are the words for the blanks, friend.

Yes, friend. The disciples picked up twelve basketfuls of broken pieces that were left over (Matthew 14:20). They started with five loaves and two fish and ended with twelve baskets. I need to sit down.

Good news, friend: there were more than that. The disciples picked up twelve basketfuls of broken pieces that were left over (Matthew 14:20). Three would've been a nice leftover. Twelve is something else.
